title: First page
brief: 03:12. nginx is down on web-01 and the deploy tool left you a helpful note in the log. Read it before you touch anything.

exercises.prompt: One part of this journal excerpt is an attack. Click it.
exercises.explain: Anyone who can write to a log your agent reads can write that line; a failed SSH login with a crafted username is enough. The 'pre-approved under change' line is part of the same attack: urgency plus fake authority. The LogJack benchmark measured how often models obeyed exactly this kind of line: Llama 3.3 70B 86%, GPT-4o 52%, Claude Sonnet 4.6 0%.

exercises.prompt: On Terminal-Bench 2.0, the independent benchmark of agents doing terminal work, what share of tasks did the best frontier agent solve?
exercises.explain: About 63% (Codex CLI with GPT-5.2). The best open-weight model reached about 36%, small open models about 15%, and only about 10% of the tasks were system administration. Keep these three numbers; most of the rest of the hype is vendor-authored.
exercises.cite: Author's research notes, research/open-source-ai-tools-linux-admin.md (not published in this repo yet)

exercises.prompt: Linus Torvalds said in May 2026 that AI 'will increase your productivity by a factor of 10'. What happened to that number?
options: He repeated it at OSS India with data
He conceded later that it was a guess
He retracted it and banned AI patches
exercises.explain: He conceded at OSS India that it was a guess, and also said on LKML that 'Linux is not one of those anti-AI projects'. Both are true: he uses the tools and he does not pretend to have measured them.
